texts.94d456ab0e4b: Objective for processing: The overall aim in the full project is to develop an approach based upon economic modelling and using routinely-collected NHS data, which allows the evaluation of the cost-effectiveness and efficiency of particular configurations of liaison psychiatry service for specified target populations. The purpose of the currently-proposed sub-project is to provide comparative data to the main study sites in the full proposal. Processing activities: This data capture the admission details for two specific hospitals in Birmingham over a 5 year period to facilitate their comparison. The data supplied will solely be used for the purpose outlined within this agreement. Specific outputs expected, including target date: (1) Academic paper to a health services research or mental health journal submitted within 6 months of data receipt. (2) Use of data in final report of main project due at end of 2017. (3) Discussion paper for mental health service commissioners. All outputs will consist of aggregate data with small numbers suppressed in line with the HES Analysis Guide. No record level data will be shared with any third party. Expected measurable benefits to health and/or social care including target date: The results of this application will be used to determine the cost-effectiveness and efficiency of a particular liaison psychiatry service configuration. Benefits include: (1) Illustration of a value of a particular approach (interrupted time series) in evaluating impact of new services. (2) Recommendation to commissioners on an approach to evaluating services using routine data.
